To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of activations in random neural networks with a wide number of hidden neurons can be mapped exactly onto lattice models in the statistical physics of disordered systems, that these lattice models can be systematically approximated in the wide network regime, and that the resulting effective field theories can be solved analytically.

random networks are equivalent to lattice models, the factorial approximation is an approximation to the lattice model, the wide network approximation is an approximation of the factorial approximation, and the effective field theory approximation is an approximation in the wide network approximation.

the distribution of the pre-activations of wide random neural nets can be exactly mapped to a lattice model in statistical field theory and that the large scale behavior is described by a Gaussian effective field theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the statistical properties of the outputs of random neural networks.
a correspondence between random neural networks and statistical field theory.
a correspondence between random neural networks and statistical field theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a random neural network is a lattice field theory.
the random neural networks are described by an effective field theories, which can be derived from statistical physics.
the distribution of the pre-activations of random neural networks can, in principle, be exactly mapped onto the lattice models of statistical physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
random neural networks can, in principle, be analyzed using the same methods as are routinely applied to lattice models in statistical field theory.
the large-scale behavior of a wide random neural network can be mapped onto the large-scale behavior in the statistical field theory.

the distribution of the pre-activations of random neural networks can, in the wide network regime, be approximated by a diagonalizable Gaussian with covariance between the hidden layers of the network and that this approximation can be systematically improved by an effective field theoretic approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a number of previous investigations of random networks have implicitly used an approximation which can now be understood and improved upon.
random neural networks may be studied using the same theoretical methods as have long been used to study statistical models in physics.
a number of recent results about random neural networks may be understood as consequences of the central limit theorem.
